newsitem.title: UK: LME metals extend gains ahead of long weekend.
newsitem.headline: LME metals extend gains ahead of long weekend.

text.p: LME copper settled at firmer levels on Thursday afternoon in low-key activity as players squared their books ahead of the four-day Easter holiday.
The bounce in copper pulled the others off morning lows and into positive territory by the end of official business.
Three months copper finished the afternoon kerb $20 firmer at $2,372 per tonne after probing as low as $2,343 in the morning and stretching up to $2,375 after lunch.
Much of the move up appeared to be short-covering as players adjusted positions, with the market basically in a holding pattern ahead of the long weekend, analysts said.
The beginning of a new quarter and the LME options declaration on April 2 should give some new impetus to the market when players return, they added.

The market remains divided as to copper's next move, with some participants believing it still needs to do more exploration of its lower range around $2,300 and others expecting further stock falls and tightness will embolden moves above $2,400.
The premium of cash over three months metal ended the day slightly firmer around $58/$60.
The others metals largely followed copper's lead.
Aluminium ended the day $10 firmer at $1,642 after touching a low of $1,627.

Despite the stronger close, prices remain below the 30-day and 10-day moving averages as well as the short-term downtrend, chartists said. Prices may have further to go on the downside before marching back to challenge the $1,700 level.
Nickel broke above the $7,800 level, ending $170 stronger at $7,805 after probing down to $7,580 in the morning.

A potential reverse head and shoulders formation was appearing in the market, and if a neckline around $7,600 was convincingly breached, prices could dive to $7,300/400, broker Brandeis said in a commentary.
Zinc finished $6 stronger at $1,295, making an impressive recovery from a morning dip to $1,260.
Lead added $6 to $686 and tin gained $60 to $5,885.
